Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation task; no cognitive reappraisal or other regulation instruction), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli—resting-state with eyes closed), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or viewing contrasts reported), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise maps reported). The article is a complete full-text report of a resting-state sDCM connectivity study and thus does not address the meta-analysis objective of task-based emotion regulation with visual stimuli. Full text appears complete for screening purposes (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Full text reports an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (DECREASE vs LOOK) during presentation of visual IAPS images (static pictures). Sample and methods are appropriate; within-task regulation contrasts (decrease-negative > look-negative) and unregulated viewing contrasts (look-negative > look-neutral) are reported. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FWE-corrected maps and peak coordinates cited). Full article (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This full-text fMRI study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) that instructs emotion regulation strategies including cognitive reappraisal (up- and down-regulation) and distraction (I6). Emotional stimuli are visual static pictures (IAPS and internet images) (I7). The sample (healthy adult females) is an eligible participant group (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation and unregulated viewing (e.g., down-regulation > look, up-regulation > look, look aversive > look neutral) (I9). Group-level whole-brain analyses were conducted and reported (exploratory whole-brain results and MNI coordinates are provided for multiple contrasts), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I10). Results and whole-brain/ROI findings are described in text and tables/supplements (I11). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion-regulation task (affect labeling: Label > Observe contrasts) with visual stimuli (faces). The paper reports within-task contrasts for negative and positive emotion regulation (NegLabel > NegObserve), conducts whole-brain voxelwise analyses (PPI whole-brain regressions and whole-brain activation regressions) with cluster correction and reports cluster results/coordinates (tables/figures), and includes an eligible sample (adolescent participants). Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (face images) with group-level whole-brain analyses and reported peak coordinates, it does not test an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (criterion I6). The task is affect labeling (label the emotion) rather than an instruction to regulate (e.g., reappraise, accept, distance, or otherwise up-/down-regulate emotion). The main reported contrast (affect label > gender label) is not an instructed regulation > look contrast nor a passive viewing (emotion > baseline) contrast as specified in I9. Therefore it fails the key eligibility requirements for this review (I6 and I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I10, I11. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I9. Full text appears complete.

Full-text reports a task-based fMRI study using instructed cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise vs Look conditions) with visual IAPS images, single-trial/block contrasts (Look-Negative>Look-Neutral; Reappraise>Look-Neutral), and a whole-brain voxelwise group-level analysis reporting MNI peak coordinates and cluster-corrected results. The sample includes a clinical GAD group and healthy controls with results reported separately. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; therefore complete. Meets all inclusion criteria I5–I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is an empirical task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs a cognitive emotion regulation strategy (distancing reappraisal) during stimulus presentation (I6). The emotional stimuli are visual IAPS images (I7). The sample includes a participant group (male marijuana users) with matched controls and reports group-level results (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation and unregulated viewing (e.g., "distance > baseline", "spontaneous_negative > baseline") (I9). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-level FWE and peak coordinates are reported in standard (MNI) space (I10), and results are clearly described in text, figures, and coordinate lists (I11). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not non-empirical (E3), not ROI-only (E4), not connectivity-only without task activation (E5), not only between-group contrasts without within-group effects (E6), and not an empathy/perspective paradigm without emotion-regulation instruction (E7).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use cognitive reappraisal (reappraise > attend contrast) while viewing visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise Negative > Attend Negative; View Negative > View Neutral) and whole-brain group-level analyses with tables of activation peaks and ROI analyses. The sample (high-risk and control young women) is acceptable. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The full text meets all required inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs a cognitive reappraisal strategy (distancing) during stimulus viewing (I6), uses visual stimuli (IAPS and photographs) (I7), includes a developmental sample (ages 6–23) which is an eligible sample (I8), reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reappraisal/Negative > Reactivity/Negative) (I9), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and thresholds (I10,I11). The manuscript includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears to be a complete full text. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore I recommend inclusion.

This full-text reports a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise vs. Maintain) using visual IAPS images, in a clinical sample (anxiety and depression). The paper reports within-task contrast Reappraise>Maintain and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise regression analyses with peak MNI coordinates and cluster thresholds. Methods, results, and discussion are present, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-task effects, and is not an empathy/perspective-taking-only design). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The full text describes a task-based fMRI study using instructed cognitive reappraisal (and related reappraisal strategies) with visual social-affective images (IAPS and similar). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (reappraise > look-negative; look-negative > reappraise; look-negative > look-neutral) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (with thresholds and cluster results) and ROI small-volume correction for the amygdala; results for patients and healthy controls are reported separately. The manuscript includes complete Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion sections. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed emotion regulation (engagement vs. distraction) with whole-brain group analyses and within-task contrasts, but the emotional stimuli are auditory (audiotaped stories) rather than visual images or videos. This violates inclusion criterion I7 (stimuli must be VISUAL). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded on the basis of not meeting I7.

This paper reports a task-based fMRI study (Study 2) using an instructed cognitive reappraisal task (regulate vs experience vs observe) with visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). It includes adults from a clinical (gambling disorder patients) and healthy control groups and provides within-task contrasts (‘regulate’ > ‘experience’, ‘experience’ > ‘observe’) and within-group activation maps. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak MNI coordinates (e.g. x = -60, y = 20, Z = 32) and cluster thresholds, meeting whole-brain reporting criteria. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This article reports an empirical, task-based fMRI experiment in which participants were explicitly instructed to perform cognitive reappraisal (interpretation/reinterpretation via contextual titles) of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures). The sample (young adult university participants) is eligible. The fMRI analysis includes within-task contrasts related to regulation (IAPS2–IAPS1 for up-/down-regulation) and reports group-level whole-brain activation results with peak coordinates (e.g., left middle temporal gyrus coordinates provided; Table 2 referenced). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not review-only, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group without within-task effects, not an empathy task lacking regulation instructions). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for the meta-analysis.

This study should be excluded because the emotional stimuli regulated were written, personally-relevant worry statements (word/sentence stimuli presented on screen). Inclusion criterion I7 requires visual emotional stimuli such as images or film/video; the review explicitly excludes studies whose regulated stimuli are word and sentence stimuli. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation including acceptance), I8 (sample qualifies—clinical GAD sample reported), I9 (reports within-task regulation contrasts, e.g., Accept > Worry, Suppress > Accept), I10 (group-level second-level random-effects analyses with reported peak coordinates), and I11 (coordinates/whole-brain results described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered based on the full text provided. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded because inclusion criterion I7 is not met (regulated stimuli were word/sentence-based rather than visual images/videos).

This study meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation — cognitive reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli: IAPS images and face photographs), I8 (clinical sample qualifies), and I9 (reports within-task contrasts such as Reappraise > Maintain and Look contrasts). However, it does NOT provide a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or peak coordinates; analyses are ROI-based using AAL masks and the authors state no conclusions can be made at the whole-brain level. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports ONLY ROI results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Inclusion criterion I10 (whole-brain evidence) is not met. Full text appears complete.

This study used an implicit/incidental reappraisal manipulation (prior descriptions) but participants were not explicitly instructed to use an emotion regulation strategy. Inclusion criterion I6 requires that an emotion regulation strategy be instructed; that requirement is not met. All other relevant inclusion criteria are satisfied: task-based fMRI (I5), visual stimuli (I7), eligible sample (I8), within-task regulation-related contrast (NNEG-DESC > NEG-DESC) reported (I9), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates reported (I10), and acceptable reporting of whole-brain results (I11). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it fails to meet I6 (no instructed regulation).

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs participants in two regulation-related conditions (attention shifting: indoor/outdoor; appraisal/labeling: like/dislike) in addition to an implicit viewing condition. Stimuli are visual static composite images (faces/scenes). Participants are healthy adults. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (male/female–face-only; indoor/outdoor–male/female; like/dislike–male/female) and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates (MNI) and FWE correction. Full article includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This full text reports an original, task-based fMRI experiment in which participants were explicitly instructed to use cognitive reappraisal (Increase/Decrease) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). It includes behavioral and physiological validation, within-task contrasts (e.g. Increase > Look-Negative; Decrease > Look-Negative), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported thresholds/coordinates. The methods, results, and discussion are complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The full text describes a task-based fMRI experiment in which participants were instructed to use emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) while viewing visual stimuli (Chinese Affective Picture System images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraisal vs. watch; suppression vs. watch; watch-negative vs. watch-neutral) and group-level whole-brain analyses with peak MNI coordinates and FWE-corrected thresholds, along with ROI/SVC analyses. Methods (participants, stimuli, fMRI acquisition, preprocessing, GLM) and results (behavioral, activation, PPI) are fully reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not only ROI-only, not only connectivity, empirical, includes within-task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is a resting-state fMRI seed-based connectivity study using an acute tryptophan depletion challenge; it does not include any task-based emotion regulation paradigm or visual emotional stimuli. Exclusion criteria: E5 applies (reports ONLY resting-state/seed-based connectivity analyses without any task activation maps). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample description qualifies). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not task-based fMRI), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli task), I9 (no within-task regulation or viewing contrasts), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked group-level activation map). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper must be excluded from this meta-analysis focused on task-based emotion regulation fMRI.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive self-distancing/reappraisal) while participants view visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures). The methods describe standard SPM8 whole-brain preprocessing and GLM contrasts (e.g., US-Paired: CER>NoCER) used to define PFC seeds and report ROI coordinates (ventral striatum center x=26,y=6,z=-8), and the Results present within-task regulation contrasts and connectivity effects. The full text includes introduction, detailed methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). No exclusion criteria apply (no non-empirical article, not limited to only ROI/connectivity without whole-brain task maps, and within-task contrasts are reported). Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of instructed emotion regulation of visual stimuli.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use cognitive reappraisal (maintain vs. reappraise) while viewing visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g. aversive-reappraise > aversive-maintain), presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-thresholding and figures/tables (with supplementary materials), and reports results for both high-EXT and low-EXT groups separately. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use distraction (MEMORIZE condition) versus passive viewing to regulate emotional responses to visual stimuli (IAPS and EmoPics), with female BPD patients and control groups reported separately. The analysis includes within-task contrasts (NEGATIVE>NEUTRAL; MEMORIZE vs VIEW) and group×time×task contrasts, and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI peak coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (positive and minimizing reappraisal) using visual stimuli (IAPS images). The sample is healthy adults, analyses include within-task contrasts (e.g., reappraise > natural), and the paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in standard space. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study with instructed emotion regulation (conscious ‘imagine’ and spontaneous suppression priming), visual stimuli (colored squares as CS+ vs CS–), an appropriate sample, and within-task contrasts (threat>safe; suppression-primed vs unprimed), the reported results are based on region-of-interest (bilateral amygdala) percent signal change analyses. The paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps or peak coordinates in standard space; analyses and inferences rely on ROI extraction only. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (ROI-only results) and fails inclusion criterion I10 (whole-brain evidence). Full text appears complete.

The full text reports a task-based fMRI study using an explicit cognitive reappraisal instruction (ERT: Reappraise, Maintain, Look) with visual IAPS images. It includes a combat-exposed PTSD and control sample with results reported separately, and presents within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraise > Maintain, Maintain > Look). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak MNI coordinates and tables; small-volume correction was applied for the amygdala but whole-brain maps and coordinate tables are provided. The manuscript contains complete sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus all relevant inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs emotion regulation (Reappraise > Maintain in the ERT) and includes unregulated viewing contrasts (Maintain > baseline, Fearful > Happy). Stimuli are visual (IAPS pictures and emotional faces). The paper reports within-task contrasts and describes voxel-wise, group-level whole-brain analysis with cluster correction and reports peak coordinates for DLPFC (x,y,z = −40,12,28), satisfying whole-brain reporting. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (Increase/Decrease) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (static angry face photographs). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Decrease > Observe-angry, Increase > Observe-angry), whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and tables, and provides full methods, results, and discussion. Sample is healthy adults and resting-state subset is reported but task analyses meet meta-analysis objectives. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (instructed to reappraise vs view/maintain) using visual stimuli (negative and neutral pictures). It reports within-task regulation contrasts (reappraise > view; regulation×time interactions) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI peak coordinates and cluster statistics, alongside ROI results. The sample includes BPD patients and healthy controls with separate group results and responder/nonresponder analyses. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and supplemental material is not required to verify core criteria. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The article reports an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use a cognitive reappraisal strategy (distancing) during presentation of visual negative and neutral pictures, satisfying I5–I7. The sample is healthy adult participants (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (RegulateNeg > WatchNeg and WatchNeg > RegulateNeg) and associated behavioral ratings (I9). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are presented with peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction (I10), and results are reported in text/figures/tables (I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the study includes whole-brain activation results (not ROI-only), is not a non-empirical paper, and does not report only connectivity or only between-group contrasts. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI emotion regulation with visual stimuli.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly matches the review objective. It instructs cognitive emotion regulation (socially-induced reappraisal/distancing) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures), reports within-task contrasts (Social-Reg > Social-Look; Self-Reg > Self-Look), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) using visual stimuli (96 IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reappraise vs Maintain, Maintain vs Look) and provides peak coordinates (MNI) for activation and connectivity results, satisfying whole-brain, voxelwise reporting. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, imaging acquisition/analysis), Results (behavioral and fMRI), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructs cognitive reappraisal of visual (IAPS) images and reports within-task contrasts and behavioral validation; however, the full text reports primarily ROI and seed-based (gPPI) connectivity analyses (L amygdala seed → R IFG) and does not present a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation map (peak coordinates for a reappraise>watch type contrast) in the main article. The paper focuses on PPI connectivity and ROI-extracted beta coupling estimates, and refers to prior work and Supplement for broader results. Because the review requires at least one whole-brain task-evoked statistical map, this paper meets exclusion criterion E5 (only seed-based/ connectivity analyses reported without a whole-brain task activation map) and therefore must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (whole-brain evidence).

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed cognitive reappraisal (Increase and Decrease) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (film clips), satisfying the intervention/strategy requirement. Stimuli were visual (first-person extreme sports film clips). The sample (healthy adult participants) is eligible. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation (e.g., Increase + Decrease vs Look-Sports) and provides group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with tables/figures of peak coordinates. Although DCM/effective connectivity analyses are included, whole-brain activation results are also reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; includes within-group task effects; not an empathy-only task). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of instructed cognitive reappraisal using visual stimuli in children (meets I5, I6, I7, I8), the published results focus exclusively on seed-based task functional connectivity (PPI) analyses and do not report any group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps or peak coordinates in standard space. This study therefore reports only seed-based connectivity/effective connectivity results without accompanying whole-brain activation maps, which meets exclusion criterion E5. Inclusion criteria I9 and I10 (within-task whole-brain activation contrasts and whole-brain peak coordinates) are not satisfied in the provided full text.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS) presented as distractors during a delayed working-memory task. The paper reports unregulated viewing contrasts (negative emotional > scrambled) and within-group as well as between-group whole-brain, voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates (FWE-corrected), and provides full methods, results and discussion. The sample includes OCD patients and matched healthy controls with within-group effects reported. Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction (e.g., reappraisal) was given, the meta-analysis objective allows inclusion of studies that view emotional stimuli without regulating; the study therefore provides an appropriate unregulated emotion contrast for inclusion. Connectivity analyses (DCM) are present but whole-brain task activations are also reported, so exclusion criterion E5 does not apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This full text describes an empirical, task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts indexing emotion generation (Maintain>Observe) and regulation (Regulate>Maintain), and presents group-level analyses and peak coordinates (including one-sample/group activation maps used to create masks and reported peak coordinates and MNI values for seeds). Although some between-group tests used masks, group-level task activation maps and coordinate peaks are reported, and PPI connectivity is supplemental rather than the sole analysis. Sample and exclusions are described and a control group is reported separately. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI/small-volume results or only connectivity analyses) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the record is complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (Increase, Decrease, Look) during visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures and high-arousal film clips). It reports within-task contrasts (Increase>Look, Decrease>Look, Increase>Decrease), presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and FWE correction, and includes methods, results, and discussion. All review inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) during presentation of visual stimuli (complex social images/IAPS). It reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., reappraise > look-negative, look-negative > reappraise) and unregulated viewing contrasts (look-negative > look-neutral). Group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported with voxelwise FDR correction and MNI coordinates/tables. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

All inclusion criteria are met: This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs a cognitive emotion regulation strategy (self-distancing/reappraisal) (I6). Regulated stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (I7). Sample is healthy participants (female young adults), qualifying under sample criteria (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Response: Attend > Distance; Prediction Error: Distance > Attend) (I9). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise with cluster-level FWE correction and reported coordinates/tables (MNI coordinate(s) and Table S2 referenced), satisfying whole-brain evidence (I10) and acceptable reporting (I11). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, etc.). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) of visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraise Negative > Attend Negative) and an unregulated viewing contrast (Attend Negative > Attend Neutral). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates and FWE cluster correction. Sample (n=62 young adults) is eligible. Although resting-state analyses are also included, the paper clearly contains task activation results, so no exclusion criteria are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) using an instructed emotion-regulation paradigm (cognitive reappraisal; I6) with visual stimuli (static IAPS pictures; I7). The sample includes unmedicated panic-disorder patients and healthy controls with results reported (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (e.g., Reappraise vs Maintain, Maintain vs Reappraise; I9). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with standard-space coordinates and Z-values (MNI peaks cited; I10/I11). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Given the clear match to the review objective (fMRI emotion regulation to visual stimuli) and the presence of whole-brain task contrasts, the study should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (‘Think Objectively’ vs ‘Watch’) using visual IAPS images in a within-subject randomized design. The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise negative > watch negative) and second-level group analyses with peak activations and cluster statistics (tables/figures; seed coordinate [−20 −4 −20] and cluster extents reported), and reports voxelwise functional connectivity (gPPI) results linked to behavior. Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10 and I11. No exclusion criteria apply (no non-empirical paper, not ROI-only, reports within-task contrasts, not resting-state-only, and includes explicit regulation instructions). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (reappraise vs attend), using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures), with both an at-risk clinical group and healthy controls whose results are reported separately. The analyses include within-task contrasts for regulation (Reappraisal > Attend Negative) and unregulated viewing (View Negative > View Neutral), performed as group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported peak MNI coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, reports within-task effects, not purely perspective-taking). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in which participants were instructed to use an emotion-regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal via distancing) while viewing visual stimuli (IAPS and matched photographs). The sample (ages 10.5–22.9) is eligible. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (regulation/negative > reactivity/negative) and unregulated viewing (reactivity/negative > reactivity/neutral), and conducts whole-brain group-level analyses with peak coordinates in standard (MNI) space. Reporting of coordinates and methods is detailed in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, includes task activation maps, not connectivity-only, not an empathy task). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly instructs cognitive reappraisal (DECREASE vs LOOK) using visual stimuli (IAPS images) and reports within-task regulation contrasts. The sample (healthy adult participants) is eligible. The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates and FWE-corrected results (including amygdala and vlPFC) and includes tables/figures/supplemental material describing whole-brain results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs explicit emotion regulation strategies (Compassion meditation and Reappraisal) during an emotion-regulation task (preparation and implementation periods). Stimuli are visual (film clips). Participants are a qualifying sample (adult meditators). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Compassion > Watch-Negative, Reappraisal > Watch-Negative) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-level correction, with results presented in tables/figures. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; reports within-group effects; not purely perspective-taking without regulation).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and acceptance) during presentation of visual sad images (IAPS and normed photos). The sample includes remitted MDD and control participants with separate group analyses. The paper reports within-task contrasts (accept > reappraise, accept > view, reappraise > view) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with reported cluster results/locations in tables and text. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Although an a priori mask/SVC was noted for some analyses, whole-brain clusters outside frontal/amygdala (e.g., insula) are reported, supporting whole-brain task-evoked results. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use two emotion-regulation strategies (Observe — a mindfulness/acceptance instruction — and Suppress) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Suppress-negative vs. Look-negative; Observe-negative vs. Look-negative; Look-negative vs. Look-neutral) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and thresholding described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the review (task-based fMRI, instructed regulation, visual stimuli, any sample, within-task contrasts, whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative emotions evoked by visual IAPS images. It reports within-task contrasts (regulate > view), performs group-level whole-brain GLM analyses with results transformed to Talairach space and provides activation coordinates (Tables/Figures). Sample (healthy adults) is acceptable. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation that instructs cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise-Neg vs Maintain-Neg), uses visual stimuli (static facial images), reports within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation, and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported activations/coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to apply emotion-regulation strategies (mindfulness and a cognitive reappraisal “reality checking”) during the anticipation and perception of emotional pictures. Stimuli were visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., exp ng > nt, per ng > nt), presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and tables/figures of activations, and provides full Methods, Results, and Discussion. Sample is healthy adults. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10 and I11. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (psychological distancing) during anticipation and stimulus periods, using visual IAPS social images. The sample includes avoidant patients and healthy controls reported separately. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation and unregulated viewing (e.g. Reappraise Cue>Look Cue, Reappraise Negative>Look Negative, Look Negative>Look Neutral) and provides group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates (text and supplemental tables/figures). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

The full text reports a task-based fMRI study using instructed affect-labeling (an implicit emotion-regulation manipulation) and an affect-matching (unregulated viewing) task with visual stimuli (photographs of emotional faces). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (affect label > gender label) and viewing (affect match > shape match). Participants include clinical (SP subgroups) and healthy control groups with group-level SPM analyses normalized to standard space; peak coordinates and whole-brain main effects are reported (supplementary table). The methods, results, and discussion are present and complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only analyses, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is a task-based fMRI study (N=51) that instructed explicit emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and suppression) while participants viewed visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to the review (View Negative > View Neutral; Reappraise > Attend Negative; Suppress > Attend Negative) and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates and tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-task effects, not an empathy/perspective-taking-only design). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria I5–I11 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed emotion regulation (reappraisal and distraction) while presenting visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation (reappraisal vs view; distraction vs view; emotion vs neutral) and describes group-level analyses. The methods state that results were thresholded and that results significant at whole-brain FWE-corrected P<0.05 are reported, and the paper describes peak activations and connectivity differences across groups; coordinates are likely provided in tables/figures/supplementary materials per the journal format. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; not limited to ROI-only or connectivity-only results; within-task effects are reported). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete for screening.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study that directly examines instructed emotion regulation (reappraise > look) and uninstructed viewing (look negative > look neutral) using visual IAPS images. It reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > look; look negative > look neutral) at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and thresholding, and presents coordinate-based results. Sample is healthy adults. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper meets several inclusion criteria (I5: task-based fMRI; I6: instructed emotion regulation with reappraisal and selective attention; I7: visual stimuli — 40 s negative film clips; I8: acceptable sample including younger and older adults; I9: reports within-task contrasts related to regulation, here as PPI contrasts such as reappraisal > passive viewing and reappraisal > selective attention). However, it violates key requirements: the article reports only seed-based functional connectivity (PPI) analyses conducted within an a priori PFC/amygdala mask and does not present a group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation map with peak coordinates in standard space (I10 not met). Therefore exclusion criteria E5 (reports ONLY seed-based/effective connectivity without a whole-brain task activation map) and E4 (reports only ROI/small-volume-masked results with no whole-brain analysis) apply. Note: the authors state that neural activity contrasts were reported previously (Allard & Kensinger, 2014), but those whole-brain activation results are not presented in this full text. Full text appears complete for this paper. Given E4 and E5, the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use emotion regulation strategies (Detachment, Reinterpretation, Distraction, Expressive Suppression) while viewing visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., ‘Regulate Negative’ > ‘Permit Negative’ and vice versa), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and FWE-corrected results, and presents full methods, results, and discussion. Sample (healthy adults) is eligible. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The full text reports an original, task-based fMRI experiment using an instructed emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) with visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). Participants include clinical (PTSD) and combat-exposed control groups with group-level analyses reported separately. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraise > Maintain) and unregulated viewing contrasts (Maintain > Look), and provides whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates and corrected thresholds. The manuscript includes complete methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructed emotion regulation (look, increase, decrease) using cognitive reappraisal strategies (I6). Stimuli were visual (IAPS and in-house disgusting images) (I7). The sample includes children/adolescents with ASD and TD controls (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (decrease-gross vs. look-gross; increase-gross vs. look-gross) (I9). It performed group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM analyses and references coordinate tables/figures (Table S2, figures) satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is empirical with original fMRI task activation maps (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only), and includes within-group task effects. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (reappraise > look contrasts) and reports within-task contrasts. Stimuli include visual faces (fearful and neutral) used during the instruction/regulation period; although top-down generation used sentences as background, the regulated stimulus during instruction is a visual face, so the study meets the visual-stimuli requirement. The sample (healthy adult women) is acceptable. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and tables/figures of activations and coordinates. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies I5–I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs a cognitive reappraisal (Regulate) strategy versus a control (Attend) during a sequential investment task. The stimuli are visual market displays presented on-screen and evoke emotional/regret responses related to financial decisions. The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing Regulate and Attend and presents group-level whole-brain analyses with reported coordinates (MNI) and thresholding, plus tables in Supporting Information. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

Study 2 reports a task-based fMRI experiment using instructed cognitive reappraisal ("CHANGE" vs "LOOK") during presentation of visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (look negative > look neutral; decrease negative > look negative) and group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates reported (Table 5). Participant groups (DSH and depression control) are reported separately. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Thus all required inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study should be excluded because the emotional stimuli being regulated are non-visual (anticipation of somatosensory pain via intraepidermal electrical stimulation), which fails inclusion criterion I7 (stimuli must be VISUAL). The study does meet multiple inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed cognitive reappraisal during anticipation), I8 (eligible sample: healthy participants reported separately), I9 (reports within-task contrasts related to regulation, e.g., regulation vs. anxiety), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), and I11 (results/coordinates described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded due to not meeting I7 (non-visual regulated stimuli).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in which children (8–12 yrs) were instructed to use a cognitive reappraisal strategy (“MAKE-POSITIVE”) while viewing visual sad images (IAPS and child-appropriate photos). The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise sad vs. view sad; view sad vs. view neutral) and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (with corrected thresholds) as well as ROI analyses. Core article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I5–I11). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use self-focused cognitive reappraisal (distancing, increase, decrease) while viewing visual IAPS images. It reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (DistA > PermA; IncA > PermA) and an unregulated viewing contrast (PermA > PermN). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported with cluster-level correction and coordinate tables. The sample includes a clinical group (SAD) and matched controls with separate group analyses. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructed participants to voluntarily generate (up-regulate) a positive mood while viewing visual stimuli (happy facial expressions) and using autobiographical memory. It reports within-task analyses using activation during the happy mood induction blocks (regression of PANAS change with brain activation), group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM results with MNI peak coordinates and cluster tables, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. All inclusion criteria relevant to the review are met (task-based fMRI, instructed regulation/up-regulation during visual stimuli, visual stimuli used, eligible sample, within-task activation/contrast analyses, and whole-brain coordinate reporting). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The full text reports a task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal: “Decrease” vs. “Look”), with visual stimuli (negative and neutral images). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (Regulate Negative vs. Look Negative) and also whole-brain group-level analyses (whole-brain effects and tables/figures reported, with coordinates in supplements). Sample and analyses meet inclusion requirements. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study fits the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria.

This study meets several inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5), explicitly instructs emotion regulation strategies including cognitive reappraisal and selective attention (I6), uses visual emotional stimuli in the form of film/video clips (I7), includes an eligible sample of younger and older adults (I8), and reports within-task contrasts comparing regulation and passive viewing (I9). However, all reported activation analyses were conducted within an explicit amygdala–PFC mask (region-limited search space), and the paper does not present a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation analysis with peak coordinates in standard space. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement (I10) and appears to report only region-of-interest / small-volume–restricted results, triggering exclusion criterion E4. Full text appears complete. Because I10 is not met and E4 applies, the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (volitional emotion regulation) using visual IAPS pictures. It reports within-task contrasts comparing Reappraise versus Maintain and includes whole-brain group-level voxelwise activation analyses (activation results and tables of coordinates) and supplementary tables/figures. All relevant inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplementary materials).

Full text reports a task-based fMRI experiment in which participants were explicitly instructed to use cognitive reappraisal (Reapp Neg) versus look (Look Neg/Look Neu) to regulate responses to visual stimuli (IAPS images). The study provides within-task contrasts (Reapp Neg vs Look Neg), whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI peak coordinates and cluster thresholds, and reports group-level results. Sample (healthy adults) is acceptable. The manuscript includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an original, task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion-regulation manipulation (guided attentional distraction vs evaluation) with visual, static OCD-relevant and aversive images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (evaluation > distraction; OCD-relevant > neutral/aversive) and group-level, whole-brain analyses (with ROI follow-up), with results presented in figures and supplementary tables. Both patient and matched healthy control groups are reported separately. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-group task effects). Full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so it is complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of instructed regulation (visual stimuli) and is included.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (and affect labeling) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (Label > Observe, Reappraise > Observe, Label > Reappraise, etc.) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in standard space (SPM5, MNI coordinates). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

Full text reports a task-based fMRI experiment instructing emotion regulation (reappraisal and distraction) using visual IAPS pictures in healthy high-risk and control groups. It provides within-task contrasts (view negative > neutral; reappraisal negative > view negative; distraction positive > view positive) from second-level random-effects analyses and gives peak coordinates in MNI space for group-level contrasts. The full article (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is available. Although ROI-based correction was used, group-level voxelwise contrasts with MNI coordinates are reported, satisfying the whole-brain coordinate reporting requirement for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that explicitly used a cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) paradigm with instructed regulation (Suppress/reappraise) and a passive Observe condition. Emotional stimuli were visual IAPS pictures. The paper reports within-task contrasts of interest (Maintain>Observe and Suppress>Maintain) and describes group-level whole-brain voxel-wise analyses with correction and supplementary tables for full results/coordinates. The sample includes cocaine-dependent groups and a healthy control group with group results reported separately. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion; supplementary tables are referenced but their absence does not render the main text incomplete.

This is a task-based (event-related) fMRI study that explicitly instructed emotion-regulation strategies (reappraisal and expressive suppression) during an anticipation (cue) and stimulus (target) period. Visual stimuli were used (IAPS negative images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Target Reappraisal > Target Appraise, Cue Suppression > Cue Reappraisal) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE correction and MNI coordinates in tables. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is excluded because it does NOT meet I6: the fMRI task is affect labeling, an incidental/implicit process, not an instructed emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance). Although labeling reduces amygdala activity and is discussed as incidental regulation, participants were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses. Satisfied inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: faces), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (within-task contrasts reported), I10 (group whole-brain maps with coordinates), I11 (results clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (explicit emotion regulation) while participants view visual stimuli (negative images). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reappraisal vs. Maintain and Reappraisal vs. Fixation), provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and cluster-correction thresholds, and includes ROI analyses for the amygdala. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I5–I11) and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise vs React) and reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise > React) across three socio-emotional tasks. Two of the regulated stimulus types are visual (looming facial photographs and dynamic video clips of social criticism), which meet the review’s requirement for visual stimuli; although one task uses written autobiographical sentences, the presence of regulated visual stimuli suffices for inclusion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with thresholding and coordinates, and provides within-group and between-group task activation maps. Participant groups (SAD patients and healthy controls) are reported separately. The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10,I11) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (reappraise vs attend) of visual sad images (IAPS and other pictures) in remitted MDD and control participants. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (reappraise-sad > attend-sad), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported clusters/coordinates (tables/figures). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (increase, decrease, maintain) during recall of previously encoded visual images (IAPS). Methods report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8) with coordinates/tables and contrasts relevant to regulation (e.g., decrease>maintain, increase>maintain, conjunctions, phase-specific contrasts). Sample is healthy young adults and within-task contrasts are reported. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (mentalizing-reappraisal: up, down, look) during presentation of visual social stimuli (photos of proposers and monetary offers displayed on screen). The sample is healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., DOWN > LOOK, UP > LOOK, DOWN < LOOK < UP) and presents group-level whole-brain analyses with cluster-corrected thresholds and peak coordinates (tables/figures). Reporting meets the meta-analysis requirements for whole-brain voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task effects, and includes explicit instructions to amplify/dampen emotion). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I11 and should be included.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (detach/experience) while participants view visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Positive-Experience > Positive-Regulate; Negative-Regulate > Negative-Experience), trial-by-trial parametric analyses, and a group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis with MNI coordinates and cluster correction (tables/figures). Sample includes younger and older adults. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, sufficient for screening. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This full-text reports a task-based BOLD fMRI study that instructed participants to use cognitive reappraisal ("Reduce Emotion") vs maintain responses to negative images (I5, I6). Stimuli were visual IAPS pictures (I7). Participant groups include healthy controls and clinical groups with results reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise vs Baseline; Maintain vs Baseline; and task effects/interaction) and behavioral-fMRI relationships (I9). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are presented with cluster thresholds and peak coordinates in Talairach space (I10), and results are reported in tables/figures/supplement (I11). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; reports whole-brain task activation maps; not only connectivity or ROI-only; includes within-group task effects; not an empathy/perspective-taking study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to label affect (an instructed strategy shown to function as incidental emotion regulation), using visual stimuli (photographs of faces). The sample includes GAD patients and healthy controls with group-level analyses. The paper reports within-task contrasts (emotion vs. fixation; affect vs. gender) and longitudinal regulation-related contrasts (pre–post changes, group-by-time interactions) and provides whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-task effects, not an empathy/perspective-taking-only paradigm). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11.

Full text is complete. Met inclusion: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: facial images), I8 (eligible sample: healthy adults), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates), I11 (results reported clearly in text/tables). Not met: I6 — the task did NOT instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraise, down-regulate, accept). Instead, the Cued Emotional Conflict Task required cognitive control/response mapping (respond to actual vs. opposite emotion) and the study correlated habitual ERQ scores with task activation; participants were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses in-scanner. I9 — there is no within-task contrast that reflects an instructed emotion-regulation condition (e.g., “reappraise > look”, “down-regulate > maintain”) nor a standard unregulated viewing contrast of emotion versus baseline that maps onto passive viewing; the reported contrasts index cognitive control/conflict (opposite vs actual) rather than an explicit regulation instruction. Therefore the study does not satisfy the core requirement (I6) and is excluded.

The full text meets all required inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study that uses instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal: downregulate and upregulate) with visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The sample (healthy participants; genotype groups reported) is acceptable, and the paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (downregulate > look, upregulate > look, negative > neutral). Group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates and cluster thresholds in standard space, satisfying whole-brain evidence. The manuscript includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or empathy-without-regulation) are met.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study with an instructed reappraisal/perspective-taking regulation strategy (meets I5, I6), includes an appropriate sample (I8), reports within-task regulation-related contrasts (I9) and presents group-level whole-brain analyses/coordinates (I10, I11), it does NOT meet the required stimulus modality criterion: the emotional content consists of monetary decision outcomes and numeric gamble displays rather than visual emotional stimuli (e.g., IAPS images, faces, or film/video). Therefore inclusion criterion I7 (visual emotional stimuli) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly instructs participants to regulate emotional responses (explicit up-regulation via instructed imitation, IMT, and down-regulation via expressive suppression, eSUP) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (dynamic face video clips). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (IMT > eSUP, IMT > GND, eSUP > IMT, etc.) and conducts group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses with coordinates and cluster reporting. The sample (20 healthy adults) is acceptable, and the full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-task effects, not an empathy task without regulation). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (up- and down-regulation) during an fMRI Ultimatum Game and during IAPS training, fulfilling the review focus on instructed emotion regulation. Stimuli are visual (IAPS pictures in training and photographs of proposers/faces during the task). The manuscript reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Down > Look, Down < Look < Up, regulated decisions contrasts) and whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. Participant sample is healthy adults and methods/results/discussion are fully presented. No exclusion criteria (ROIs-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or perspective-taking without regulation) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI experiment that explicitly instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) and also includes a placebo regulation condition. Visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures) were used. The sample comprises healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g. RU–CUR, PU–CUP and related conjunction/subtraction contrasts) and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates and tables/figures in standard space. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only analyses, non-empirical paper, or empathy-only perspective tasks) are met. Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study using an instructed cognitive reappraisal emotion-regulation task (regulate vs. look) with visual stimuli (IAPS photographs). It reports within-task contrasts for emotional reactivity (negative > neutral) and reappraisal (regulate negative > look negative) with group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and MNI peak coordinates (whole-brain FWE correction for regulate>look). Sample and analyses meet inclusion requirements. The full text is complete (background, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/ connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and not an empathy without regulation task).

Exclusion E4 applies: the study reports primarily ROI/mask-based voxelwise analyses (a priori ROIs: left/right amygdala and insula; exploratory larger ROI mask) and does not present a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map in standard space. Consequently inclusion criterion I10 (whole-brain evidence) is not met. The study does satisfy: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed implicit emotion-regulation paradigm via attend/ignore instructions qualifies as instructed cognitive control), I7 (visual stimuli—faces and houses), I8 (sample reported; clinical group with controls), and I9 (within-task contrasts related to regulation/attention: attend vs ignore fearful faces and emotion×attention interactions). Because I10 is not met and E4 is triggered (ONLY ROI/mask results), the study is excluded from the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (reappraise and distract) while participants view sad images (visual stimuli). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Sad-Reappraise > Sad-View, Sad-Distract > Sad-View) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise mixed-effects analyses in MNI space with tables/figures of cluster results. The sample and analyses meet eligibility and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-only, not empathy-without-regulation). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; full text appears complete.

This article meets all inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs explicit emotion regulation strategies including cognitive reappraisal and distraction (I6). The emotional stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (I7). The sample includes remitted MDD patients and healthy controls with group-level results reported (I8). Analyses include within-task contrasts related to regulation (reappraisal vs. view; distraction vs. view) and viewing contrasts (I9). The paper reports group-level activation peaks in standard (MNI) space (e.g., amygdala coordinates) and thresholding information, consistent with whole-brain/voxelwise reporting (I10,I11). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore the study should be included.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed emotion regulation (reappraisal) using visual stimuli (IAPS images and facial displays) in an appropriate adult sample and reports within-task contrasts (Look vs Decrease; Match vs Label). However, all activation effects are reported using ROI-based analyses (amygdala ROIs) and PPI connectivity analyses restricted to anatomically defined IFG masks. The paper does not present any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps (analyses were mask-restricted), so it fails inclusion criterion I10 and (by implication) I11. This violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only ROI / small-volume-corrected results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This article meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using instructed cognitive reappraisal (I6) with visual stimuli (IAPS pictures; I7). The sample is healthy adults (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g. Reappraise > Attend; Reappraise negative > Attend negative; Attend negative > Reappraise negative) (I9). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates in MNI space and described in the text and figures (I10, I11). The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided and complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task effects, not an empathy-only paradigm).

This paper is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (decrease) versus look conditions using visual stimuli (IAPS and child-friendly pictures). The sample includes ages 10–22 (children, adolescents, young adults). The manuscript reports within-task contrasts of interest (decrease negative > look negative; look negative > look neutral), and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with thresholding and peak coordinates (tables/supplementary material). The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10 and I11. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study with explicit instructed emotion regulation (reappraisal REAP and suppression ESUP) and a natural viewing condition. Emotional stimuli are visual static images (IAPS and photos) with social/nonsocial categories. Sample includes 19 healthy adults. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., social pleasant vs nonsocial pleasant; effects during NAT, REAP, ESUP) and whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with reported peak coordinates and SPM maps. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and violates no exclusion criteria.

Full article reports an fMRI task with instructed cognitive reappraisal (distancing) during anticipation of visual reward cues (coins). Methods and analyses include within-task regulation contrasts (regulate > permit and interactions), whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and appropriate correction, and task-based design. Sample is healthy adults. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply; full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation: distancing reappraisal), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (within-task reappraisal contrasts reported, e.g., R–NR), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported MNI peak coordinates), I11 (results reported in text/tables/figures). This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (sad and neutral film clips) and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (Sad > Neutral). The study therefore meets the review’s scope (studies of viewing visual emotional stimuli without regulation) and satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in which children/adolescents were instructed to regulate emotional responses (cognitive reappraisal-style strategies: ‘pretend it’s fake’ or ‘pretend it’s right in front of you’) while viewing visual disgust-inducing images (IAPS and in-house images). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (decrease-gross > look-gross; increase-gross > look-gross) and unregulated viewing (look-gross > look-neutral). Group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported (with cluster thresholds and Talairach coordinates). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study (N=30) that explicitly instructs emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and distraction) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (reappraisal > view; distraction > view; reappraisal vs distraction), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FDR correction, and tables/figures with peak coordinates. Sample is healthy adults and the full text contains methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly instructs emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) during presentation of visual emotional images (IAPS and Internet pictures). The sample (healthy adult women) is acceptable. The paper reports within-task contrasts of regulation conditions (e.g., REAP vs ESUP, NAT vs REAP), behavioral and fMRI results, and second-level random-effects whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates and tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation that instructs cognitive reappraisal (distancing) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise > Experience; Experience > Reappraise), uses whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates and whole-brain correction, and provides full methods, results, and discussion in the full text. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This full-text reports a task-based fMRI experiment using instructed cognitive reappraisal (MAINTAIN/INCREASE/DECREASE) with visual IAPS images, includes both a patient (BPD) and healthy control group with separate reporting, presents within-task contrasts (DECREASE>MAINTAIN, INCREASE>MAINTAIN, negative>neutral), and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates/tables. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

This full text meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that includes an instructed emotion-regulation condition: affect labeling (participants verbally label facial emotions), which functions as an incidental/instructed regulation strategy (I6). The emotional stimuli are visual (static face images) (I7). The sample includes patient (methamphetamine-dependent) and control groups with results reported separately (I8).
