Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation in older adults that reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results. However, the regulated stimuli are personalized worry/suppression sentences (script-driven imagery / word/sentence prompts presented on the screen) rather than visual emotional stimuli (e.g., pictures, faces, film). Inclusion criterion I7 requires visual emotional stimuli and specifically excludes studies using word or sentence stimuli or purely script-driven imagery. Therefore the study fails to meet I7 and must be excluded. Included criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation: worry suppression), I8 (eligible sample: elderly clinical + controls), I9 (reports within-task contrasts), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise maps), I11 (results reported in text/tables). Exclusion criteria met: none.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative emotion (Reduce vs Maintain) while viewing visual stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (Reduce > Maintain and related effects), presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-correction (AlphaSim) and tables/figures of significant clusters, and includes an eligible sample (anxious and control groups). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use emotion regulation strategies (reappraise, suppress, view) while viewing visual stimuli (IAPS and in-house pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., reappraise > view, view > reappraise), behavioral and fMRI results, and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-corrected thresholds and reported activation coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not a review, and task involves instructed regulation of emotional responses). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the meta-analysis (I5–I11). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5 met) with an eligible sample (I8 met). It reports within-task emotion contrasts (unpleasant > neutral; pleasant > neutral) so unregulated viewing contrasts are available (I9 met) and it provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with tabulated results (I10 and I11 met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Because not all inclusion criteria are satisfied (specifically I6 and I7), the study is excluded.

Although this is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study using visual stimuli (IAPS) with within-task contrasts (EXP neg > neut, PRES neg > neut) and reports peak coordinates (meeting I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11), it does NOT instruct participants to implement an emotion-regulation strategy during scanning. This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (reappraisal by distancing) while participants view visual emotional stimuli (IAPS interpersonal images). This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (reinterpretation) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS images). Although this is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (partner facial expressions), reporting unregulated viewing contrasts (partner negative > partner neutral) and group-level whole-brain results with coordinates, it does NOT meet inclusion criterion I6: there was no instruction to regulate emotion (participants were explicitly not instructed to regulate). Exclusion decision: E4 applies. This study does not instruct or evaluate an emotion regulation strategy (I6 not met): the task is an implicit emotional face-matching (matching faces vs shapes) with no instructions to reappraise, distance, accept, or otherwise regulate emotional responses, and there are no within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise>look). Although it is a task-based fMRI study (I5), uses visual emotional stimuli (faces) (I7), includes an eligible sample of healthy adults (I8), and reports an unregulated viewing contrast (face-matching > form-matching) used in analysis (I9), it does not present a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation map with reported peak coordinates in standard space (I10 not met). Instead, the paper reports small-volume–corrected amygdala results and network-based connectivity (NBS) findings. Because it lacks instructed regulation and a qualifying whole-brain task activation map and reports only ROI/SVC results for task activation, it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I10 and meets exclusion criterion E4. Exclusion therefore recommended.

Because the study reports only seed-based connectivity analyses without a qualifying whole-brain task activation map, it falls under exclusion criterion E5. Therefore it must be excluded from the meta-analysis.
